Persona: imagine if banks had deposit interest rates at negative -1% ,which at this point is roughly true. So if you had 1000€ and just kept it in the bank, next year you would have 990€ - a loss of 10€. Banks at the moment are giving out loans at rates negative rates of 0.5% (so they pay you for taking the loan), which is likely to be true if deposit rates keep getting negative. 
Now the most unrelistic assumption I would also add is that it had became to take a loan out of a bank nearly as easy as from a fast credit (P2P), since, for instance, no more credit rating checking or low mortgage requirements. Therefore if interest rates (price) of P2P loans (product) are very positely high, the loaned money (quantity) of P2P loans will be 0 (supply demand rules). The market mechanism will then adjust the rates (price) to an equilibrium and it would make sense for it to be negative, for example -0.25%. Since in such economy, you will naturally lose money (-1% a year), unless you lend it to someone in which case you would lose only -0.25% a year, leaving you at 997.5€
Persona: But to some point it is reality
Persona: of course
Persona: now thats fantasy
Persona: Would be fun to theorize how the fuck would math play out and if, say commercial bank rates would negative 25% a year, then would P2P loans do a, say negative 10%. I think they would. 

Negative rate of 25% on loans means that the interest rate of deposits must be 25%+, for example 30%. So If you have 1000€ and you keep them for a year, next year you have 700€. But if you put in into P2P for negative 10%, next year you have 900€. Thats a smaller loss :) And if the world only consists of losses, a smaller loss would mean profit.
Persona: Negative interest rate economy is hella interesting
Persona: If banks are giving you a loan of 1000€ and they only ask you to return 500€ after 2 years, why the fuck would you choose some P2P that gives you 1000€ and asks for 1500€ after 2 years? (hypothetically)
No one would take the P2P loan, unless the banks are unrealistically strict in the way they give loans, which would drive demand fro P2P down, thus rates for P2P will fall too and it can be negative.
Persona: The central banks can only enforce its own rates. Commercial banks borrow its loan funding from the central banks and they loan money that they don't have. Thats why central bank interest rates directly affect the commercial banks, since if they didn't play along - they would make a huge loss. 
Banks almost always have lower interests rates than P2P, but its harder and slower to get a loan from a bank, so some people must go to P2P (or fast credits).
However, while the loan markets differ, they are still in the same category and if bank interests rate fall, P2P must be affected anyways and I think its quite direct, just P2P may always be like 10% in interest rates more than banks. 
You could hold the central bank as government as it pursues macroeconomic goals (high growth, low inflation), but the other banks are actually not pursuing such goals. THey are being indirectly influenced by the central bank, and since central bank is the main supplier of commercial banks money - the influence is pretty damn high. P2P is not that closely related to central bank, but its related to commercial banks, since they are their competition.

I simple view it as that P2P interests rates are commercial-bank-rate+10%. The 10% is of course an example number but its not that far from truth I would say. It largely depends on the country and time.

Thats how I understand, but maybe its different.
